title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space

quotes.text: SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.
quotes.for: Conditional approval by the FCC for up to 1 million satellites for orbital data centers.

quotes.text: The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.
quotes.for: Dismissal of opponents' concerns outside regulatory authority.

title: Feds Approve SpaceX’s AI Data Center Satellites, All 1 Million of Them

quotes.text: Under its new license, SpaceX must deploy its first operational Starmind satellite by November 2033.
quotes.for: Milestone requirement to deploy the first operational satellite by November 2033.

quotes.text: The company must then deploy 10% of the constellation, or 100,000 satellites, by November 2035, and 50% by November 2038.
quotes.for: Deployment milestones of 10% by 2035 and 50% by 2038.

quotes.text: The company sought a waiver to allow satellites operating above 372 miles (600 kilometers) to be moved into so-called graveyard orbits at the end of their operational lives, rather than being brought down to burn up in the atmosphere.
quotes.for: Sought waiver to move satellites operating above 600 kilometers into graveyard orbits.

title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical

quotes.text: The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.
quotes.for: Approval for 1 million satellites for data centers in space.

quotes.text: A lengthier authorization order published by the FCC noted that the company must deploy at least "one authorized space station" by 2033 — and then gradually add more and more through 2040.
quotes.for: Authorization order requirement to deploy space station by 2033 through 2040.
